# Natural PDF

> A Python library for intelligent PDF processing with jQuery-like selectors and spatial awareness.

Natural PDF combines traditional PDF parsing with modern AI capabilities. It provides a fluent API for selecting and manipulating PDF elements, with spatial navigation, OCR integration, and AI-powered extraction.

## Quick Start

- [Installation](https://jsoma.github.io/natural-pdf/get-started/): pip install natural-pdf, what each extra unlocks
- [Quickstart](https://jsoma.github.io/natural-pdf/get-started/quickstart/): Open a PDF, extract a value and a table
- [Selector Reference](https://jsoma.github.io/natural-pdf/reference/selectors/): Essential methods and patterns

## Key Concepts

### PDF Object Model
- `PDF`: Document container, access pages via `pdf.pages`
- `Page`: Single page with find/extract methods
- `Element`: Text, line, rect, image on a page
- `Region`: Rectangular area for scoped operations
- `ElementCollection`: List-like container with PDF-specific methods

### Selector Syntax
- Element types: `text`, `line`, `rect`, `image`, `region`
- Pseudo-classes: `:contains()`, `:bold`, `:italic`, `:above()`, `:below()`
- Attributes: `[size>=12]`, `[fontname*=Arial]`, `[source=ocr]`
- Aggregates: `[size=max()]`, `[x0=min()]`, `[fontname=mode()]`

### Common Methods
- `page.find(selector)` -> Element | None
- `page.find_all(selector)` -> ElementCollection
- `page.extract_text()` -> str
- `page.extract_table()` -> TableResult
- `page.extract_tables()` -> List[TableResult]
- `page.extract_anchored_rows(anchors, side='right')` -> list[AnchoredRow]
- `pdf.pages.extract_anchored_rows(anchors, side='right')` -> list[AnchoredRow]
- `page.extract_table_guided(headers, row_anchors, header_anchor=...)` -> TableResult
- `page.guides().from_headers_and_row_anchors(headers, row_anchors, header_anchor=...)` -> Guides
- `page.to_markdown()` -> str (VLM-powered)
- `pdf.search(query, top_k=5)` -> PageCollection (semantic search)
- `element.below()` / `.above()` / `.left()` / `.right()` -> Region
- `page.apply_ocr(engine='rapidocr')` -> Page
- OCR modes are recognition (default), detection (`detect_only=True`), and
  custom recognition (`function=`); `ocr_function=` is removed and rejected.
- OCR replacement modes are strict strings: `replace='ocr'` (default),
  `replace='all'`, or `replace='none'`. Booleans are rejected. Region and Flow
  replacement is limited to the processed geometry. `detect_only=True`
  refreshes prior detection-only artifacts in scope while preserving native and
  recognized text; non-default `replace` values are rejected.
- `pdf.apply_ocr(pages=..., show_progress=...)` -> PDF; collection OCR also
  accepts `max_workers=...`.
- Guide OCR is scoped through `guides.cells`, `guides.rows`, and
  `guides.columns`; use `guides.cells.plan_ocr(...)` then
  `guides.cells.apply_ocr(...)`. There is no top-level `Guides.apply_ocr`.
- Use `elements.correct_ocr(...)` for explicit OCR correction.
- `page.analyze_layout(engine='yolo')` -> ElementCollection

### Table Recovery Patterns
- If `extract_table()` misses a borderless or tiny-font native-text table, do not jump straight to OCR. First try `page.extract_table_guided(headers, row_anchors, header_anchor=...)`: use visible headers for vertical guides, stable first-column IDs/case numbers for horizontal guides, then snap vertical guides to whitespace before extracting cells. Header elements are most reliable; unique header-name strings can infer the header row, and repeated/ambiguous headers should pass `header_anchor`.
- Use `extract_anchored_rows()` when each row is keyed by a margin number, case number, row ID, or other stable visual anchor and you need same-row text to the left or right.
- Use `cell_overlap='center'` for small crowded text after the guides are placed, so cells are assigned by text centers instead of incidental bounding-box overlap.
- If one PDF text object spans adjacent values, such as two dates in neighboring columns, split that value with a pattern after extraction instead of duplicating it across cells.

### OCR Engines
- `rapidocr`: Default, lightweight ONNX models (~15MB)
- `paddle`: Fast, CPU-friendly
- `paddlevl`: VLM-based document understanding (charts, complex layouts)
- `doctr`: Document-focused OCR

### Layout Engines
- `yolo`: Fast, good for standard documents
- `tatr`: Table-focused (Microsoft Table Transformer)
- `paddle`: Lightweight layout detection
